requirements.summary: Single recovery locus: a new Store recovery method executes once per process, after storage.Open acquires the writer lock and before startup admission (Loop.Start). It never runs in Reload, mid-run saves, or ensureReplaceable; ensureReplaceable is unchanged.

Quarantinable class: any Load/LoadPrompts ErrCorrupt rejection (decode/envelope, trailing data, checksum mismatch, unsupported schema, failed Validate) and any read failure of a REGULAR file at the snapshot path are quarantinable: one atomic same-directory rename of the original file to a timestamped quarantine name before any fresh snapshot is published. Bytes are preserved exactly; no delete, truncate, or overwrite-first.

Fatal class: a non-regular file at a snapshot path (directory, device, socket — a directory cannot follow the rename rule), quarantine rename failure, and post-rename directory-sync failure are fatal: startup exits failure with code state_directory, kind resource, remediation and resource.path per the existing stateDirectoryFailure record (cmd/mcp-bridge/startup_failure.go:26-33). The typed record is the only output for the condition: arbitrary Go error text is never a log field or free-text line (docs/logging-contract.md); the class, kind and configured-path attribution carry the diagnosis. When no rename occurred, the file is untouched; a failed rename leaves the original bytes at the original path; a failed post-rename sync leaves the bytes at the quarantine path with the original absent.

Typed warning: for each quarantined file exactly one structured record, event startup_snapshot_rejected, operation startup, level warn, outcome degraded, error.code snapshot_unavailable (closed AD13 mapping, docs/logging-contract.md AD13), error.kind resource, error.retryable true, existing static remediation and message, resource.path = configured state directory (the resource object carries only configured path/listener/address attribution, docs/logging-contract.md:252, :338), plus two optional event-specific fields under the documented optional-addition rule (docs/logging-contract.md:499-512, :585-586; schema_version stays 1): failure_reason with the finite value corrupt_json | checksum_mismatch | unsupported_schema | validation_failure | read_error, and quarantine_path = the quarantined file's full path (validated: absolute path, .json suffix, base name in the snapshot.corrupt-*.json | prompts.corrupt-*.json families). The observe envelope write path accepts exactly these two extensions (internal/observe/envelope.go: failure_reason whitelist extension, quarantine_path field case); no other envelope vocabulary widens. No startup_failed or internal_error record is emitted for a quarantinable condition.

Retention bound: at most 5 quarantine files per family (snapshot.corrupt-*.json, prompts.corrupt-*.json); after each successful rename, the oldest beyond the bound is pruned. Ordering parses each name's RFC3339Nano UTC timestamp strictly (time.Parse; names matching a family glob with an unparsable or invalid timestamp, and any non-conforming directory entry, are never pruned and never counted toward the bound — foreign/operator files are never deleted). Prune failure is non-fatal and reported exactly once per affected family via a typed lifecycle record event snapshot_retention_failed, operation startup, level warn, outcome failure, error.code snapshot_unavailable, kind resource, retryable true (new AD13-table row added under the optional-addition rule; schema_version stays 1), carrying resource.path = configured state directory and optional quarantine_path naming the file that could not be removed. internal_warning is NOT used: it is pinned to operation reload and defined as a defect indicator (docs/logging-contract.md:481-488).

No-op on valid or absent snapshots: when Load/LoadPrompts succeeds or reports ErrNoSnapshot, recovery mutates nothing — no rename, no warning, no retention pass; a successfully loaded snapshot keeps its trusted state and the existing no-overwrite protection is untouched.
Prompt-snapshot coverage: prompts.json receives identical quarantine behavior with prompts.corrupt-*.json names and the same retention bound.

Operator opt-out: environment variable MCP_SNAPSHOT_QUARANTINE=off (case-insensitive comparison) disables recovery (fail-closed): no quarantine rename and no new recovery record (no startup_snapshot_rejected record carrying failure_reason/quarantine_path, no snapshot_retention_failed record). Today's wedge semantics otherwise hold: the Durable loader failure still emits the pre-existing structured startup_snapshot_rejected record (internal/service/loop.go:148-151 translated by cmd/mcp-bridge/wiring.go:485-492), the admission persist fails fatally, the startup_failed/internal_error record is emitted, and the process exits 1. Any other value, including unset, enables recovery. [OWNER-CONFIRMED 2026-11-21] default = enabled.
Machine-readable reasons: Load/LoadPrompts rejections gain errors.Is-compatible reason sentinels chained under ErrCorrupt, so every existing errors.Is(err, ErrCorrupt) caller and test is unaffected.
